newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Judge finds line-item veto law unconstitutional.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Judge finds line-item veto law unconstitutional.

text.p: A U.S. federal judge Thursday ruled a new law giving the president power to veto individual items in tax and spending bills was unconstitutional, court officials said.

The ruling by U.S. District Judge Thomas Penfield Jackson is sure to be appealed, supporters of the law said. They also predicted that the decision would have little impact on current budget negotiations in Congress.

"Rather than making expenditures of federal funds appropriated by Congress matters of presidential discretion, the act effectively permits the president to repeal duly enacted provisions of federal law. This he cannot do," Jackson said in his decision declaring the act unconstitional.
President Clinton has long supported the law, which was passed by the Republican-led Congress.
"If the decision was as reported, obviously we are disappointed, but we haven't had a chance to review it," a White House spokeswoman said.

The suit challenging the so-called line item veto law charged it violated the process laid out by the constitution for making or changing a law. Under the constitution the president has three options in dealing with laws -- he can sign or veto a bill or let it become law without a signature.
